## FLAGS — where the honest value differs from what the pack's prose implies

1. The general-sample bound in CLAUDE.md (5.17% over 483 rows) is SUPERSEDED. The artifact publishes 3.05% over 473 rows. Used the artifact.

2. "of 100" IS FALSE for 1 of the 3 findings on the Track A artifact: Ground option is listed and purchasable (99 adjudicated of 99 asked). Every peer sentence below is generated by peerSentence(), which names its own denominator.

3. THE PACK'S TRACK A ARGUMENT DOES NOT HOLD ON THIS STORE, and the number is kept rather than the copy. The pack reads "X of 100 stores state this on-page — so this is a peer gap, not a nitpick", which needs a HIGH X. On birdrockcoffee.com every unmet requirement is one MOST comparable stores also fail (11/100, 8/100, 7/99 state it). The honest framing is the opposite and is arguably stronger: this is a category-wide gap, which is an argument for the STANDARD rather than a criticism of one merchant. The line below says that instead.

**No spread may be stated between the two samples.** Their 95% intervals overlap (coffee 2.14–8.75%, general 0.45–2.45%), so no sentence may claim a
category sample and a general sample differ. That claim has been retired four times and revived
by a fix twice.

## TRACK A — the standard story (coffee / food-bev clients)

**Reference store:** birdrockcoffee.com · **Contract:** ALS-COFFEE v1.3
**Result:** 4 stated · 5 not stated · 1 not decidable publicly of 10

> **Subject:** birdrockcoffee.com — 3 things an AI can't get from their product pages
>
> Hi {NAME} — I build conformance tests for AI commerce (solo founder, engineer at heart).
> I ran birdrockcoffee.com — saw them in your portfolio — against a published buying standard
> for coffee.
>
> 3 findings, each checkable on their live page in ~30 seconds:
> - **A single-origin claim is stated in readable text** — Checked product copy, structured data, product title, variant options and page description — no statement an AI buyer could verify. 89 of 100 coffee stores don't state this either.
> - **An organic claim is stated in readable text** — Checked product copy, structured data, product title, variant options and page description — no statement an AI buyer could verify. 92 of 100 coffee stores don't state this either.
> - **Ground option is listed and purchasable** — Checked the public variant list — no "Ground" variant found. 92 of 99 coffee stores don't state this either.
>
> The part that's unusual: we publish our own error rate (9.99% 95% upper
> bound, measured over 160 passing rows read back one at a time; method public),
> version every standard, and every verdict carries the exact sentence it rests on — built so it
> can survive a client pushing back on it.
>
> I'm doing 5 conversations with agencies who write audit deliverables before deciding what to
> build next. 20 minutes: I'll run any client you pick live, and I want one answer from you —
> what would this need to output to go into a deliverable you'd sign?
>
